paper-main-classification: Nature Communications Results and Figure 2: Pax2 was highly expressed in I1-I7; I8 lacked Pax2 but shared Mpped2 with the other interneuron clusters and was initially described as a suspected rare cholinergic interneuron.

paper-methods-sample-frame: Nature Communications Methods, Single nucleus isolation and sequencing: 12 eight-week-old mice (6 female, 6 male), matching regions pooled from two mice, and three processing replicates comprising male, female, and mixed-sex tissue.

paper-interneuron-section: Nature Communications Cholinergic interneurons section and Figure 5: eight source clusters were used for the main analysis; 14 finer subclasses lacked robustly distinct markers and showed no rostrocaudal differences; I1-I4 carried Slc6a1/Mpped2 context and Piezo2 was also detected in I1 and I7.

study-missing-axes: Neither the deposited annotation object nor the retained I1-I8 evidence supplies per-nucleus xyz coordinates, neurite or soma geometry, intracellular structures, electrophysiology, projection targets, synaptic edges, SCI states, atlas transforms, or cross-source identities.

record.boundary: Counts are source-row sample membership, not xyz coordinates, segment identities, laminae, centroids, independent animals, or prevalence. Twelve source mice, four mice per processing replicate, two mice per first-stage matching-region pool, three processing replicates, nine GEO samples, and nucleus rows are distinct denominator levels. No profile-specific independent-animal denominator is recoverable from this annotation object. No morphology, internal structure, synapse, SCI state, cross-source identity, or atlas registration is admitted.
